title: Withdrawal symptoms in abstinent methamphetamine-dependent subjects

claims.statement: In 56 people with methamphetamine dependence followed during abstinence on a research ward, the commonest symptoms at entry were preoccupation with methamphetamine (72%), craving (68%), increased appetite (63%) and tiredness (56%); most symptoms, including psychotic-type ratings, fell during the first one to two weeks, depressive scores stayed above controls' for about three weeks, and craving persisted at a reduced level to week 5.
claims.magnitude: At entry (n=32): preoccupation 72%, craving 68%, increased appetite 63%, tiredness 56%; depressive symptoms (n=28) above controls for about 3 weeks, approaching controls at week 4 (p=0.07); craving (n=26) lower after 2 weeks, present to week 5.
